account:
Today I am keeping my mayoral appointments. I attended morning office hours, visited the east-bank mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, went home for lunch, and have returned to the office for thirteen hundred council letters. The mill's sale chest held 98 hay blocks and 60 emeralds, although I did not establish whether milling itself is running smoothly. The secretary reported no new correspondence or business this morning.

The unusual news is repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Several townsfolk repeated this, with one naming the baker, freight, and innkeeper as having been there. None gave a clear description of the change, its purpose, or whether anyone actually saw it. My neighbour crossed the bridge without trouble, so I have no evidence that passage is blocked or altered. It might concern transport or deliveries, but that is only a possibility, not something I know. I should seek a firsthand explanation from those named rather than treat these repetitions as confirmation.

My neighbour expects me for tea at fifteen hundred at the dockside cottage. The innkeeper has confirmed meeting me at my office at seventeen forty-five, then accompanying me to the great hall at eighteen for our scheduled discussion of the inn's service to town. The neighbour also relayed that the inn was quiet this morning and that the innkeeper spoke warmly about welcoming service. I do not know whether that meeting or the inn's business has any connection to the bakery reports.
